title: Make verifier snapshot unwritable even for root; rerun once on change
summary: The verifier runs against a snapshot it cannot write to even as root (a write deny in its grant enforced by the agent policy, plus a root-proof lock such as the immutable attribute where available). If HEAD or the tree still differs, the verdict is discarded, verification reruns once on a fresh snapshot, and a system fault is recorded instead of rejecting the work. Audience: Athena maintainers. Protection tests must prove they can fail: the write succeeds unlocked, is refused locked, and fail loudly rather than skip when the lock cannot be enforced.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for lock, rerun, fault and budget paths; fmt, clippy and test must pass.
Write protection is enforced by a grant deny and a lock, not by prose.
Prevent the write rather than only detecting it, and make tests prove they can fail.
Tests exercise the write attempt behavior directly.
Prefer existing OS facilities (immutable attribute, policy deny) over new machinery.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Athena's agents run as root, so permission bits alone do not stop writes; the enforcing mechanism must be the grant's write deny in crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs (and/or an immutable attribute or unprivileged user).
The previous attempt's work is discarded; this starts from the base and keeps the same rerun-once and system-fault semantics.
When the budget runs out before the rerun, the job's reason must report the budget failure, not 'changed its snapshot twice'.
Tests run as the same user as the verifier and never silently return early when a write succeeds.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test first shows a file edit and a git commit succeed in an unlocked snapshot under the current user, then shows both are refused once the verifier's lock/grant is applied, and that HEAD and work-tree tree are unchanged. It fails (not skips or returns early) if the write is not refused. Run: cargo test -p athena-git and cargo test -p athena-core.
The verifier-grant write deny is tested in policy: a write tool call against the snapshot path is denied even when the process is root. Run: cargo test -p athena-agent.

A fake-agent test shows a changed snapshot fingerprint after the first verifier run triggers exactly one more verifier invocation on a freshly created snapshot, and the first verdict is discarded. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

A test shows that after a changed fingerprint the outcome is recorded as a system fault and the judgment has no 'verifier changed its snapshot' blocker and does not reject the work; an unchanged snapshot runs the verifier once and uses its verdict. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
A test shows that when the budget is exhausted before the rerun, the job's reason reports the budget failure rather than 'snapshot changed twice'. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test pass on the workspace.
verify.rs no longer turns snapshot_changed into a blocker against the work, and run.rs near the old snapshot_changed branch discards the verdict and reruns once.

out_of_scope: Changes to records/ or governance files such as athena.toml and defaults.toml
departures: Larger than the reference: multi-crate change, root-proof enforcement, and a prior rejection raise cost and verification risk.
